outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 that I could confirm settles the algebraic statement or moves a case of it; every status statement I read calls it open in general. One in-window paper (Nascimento, Jorge-Pérez and Freitas, arXiv 2405.06745, May 2024) gives a conditional criterion for the ring-theoretic version, and one (Barajas, Chávez-Martínez and Romano-Velázquez, arXiv 2510.07607, October 2025) is about a different question, with its link to the conjecture unresolved from what I could read.
problem_asks: Statement: for a complex algebraic variety V with coordinate ring R (a finitely generated C-algebra), if the derivations Der_C(R) form a free R-module, then V is smooth. Unpacked: (a) the base field is C, characteristic zero; (b) the object is a complex algebraic variety V and its coordinate ring R, so the statement is global/affine as worded; (c) the hypothesis is that Der_C(R) is a free R-module, not merely projective, finitely generated, or of finite projective dimension; (d) the conclusion is that V is smooth; in local form, R is regular at each closed point, and the literature treats the two as the same statement; (e) only one implication is asked (freeness implies smoothness); the converse is not asked. Equivalences the literature uses: for affine V, Der_C(R) is the global sections of the tangent sheaf, so 'Der free' is 'tangent sheaf locally free'; Lipman's theorem that Der-freeness forces normality reduces the question to normal V. Variants that carry the same name but are not what the bullet literally states, and which I record only as scope: the analytic (complex space) version, the local and graded versions, the generalised version with reflexive p-forms, the algebraifold version with finitely generated projective Der, and the strong Herzog–Vasconcelos–Zariski–Lipman version with finite projective dimension.

events.what_happened: P. Graf, 'The generalized Lipman–Zariski problem', arXiv:1405.1244. v1 6 May 2014; v2 28 May 2014; v3 16 Oct 2014 (last). Published in Math. events.what_happened: The family is a single manuscript, 'A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf'. Its Theorem 1 (thm:main) claims that there exist a finitely generated normal integral C-algebra A of Krull dimension two and a maximal ideal m of A with Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A (free of rank two) and A_m not regular. The argument has two steps. (1) Proposition 'analytic-counterexample' builds a normal complex surface germ (X,x), smooth off x, with free holomorphic tangent sheaf of rank two. It takes a smooth genus-21 curve C with normal bundle L⁻¹, deg L = 10, L⁴ ≅ K_C; prescribes finite jets of two vector fields on a neighbourhood of C by finitely many holomorphic flows; glues these to a Hausdorff surface neighbourhood Y of C; lifts the jets holomorphically using vanishing of H¹ on the ideal filtration; and contracts C to x by Grauert's criterion. The text gives C² = −10, canonical discrepancy −5 for C, and p_g ≥ 33 (Remark 'invariants'). (2) Proposition 'algebraization' produces an affine normal A with the same completed local ring as (X,x) at the marked point, a principal affine neighbourhood on which Der_C(A) ≅ A^d with d = 2, and smoothness away from that point. The proof uses a finite-determinacy lemma with a relation matrix, which the paper proves itself, together with Artin approximation over a henselization.
events.delivers: Disproves the statement as listed, in its affine form. The claim is a normal affine complex surface Spec A whose coordinate ring has free derivation module Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A, and which is singular at m because A_m is not regular. The manuscript says the result 'disproves the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero'. Its formulation matches the list: Der_C(A) is Hom_A(Ω¹_{A/C}, A), the hypothesis is freeness of the whole module, and the conclusion (smoothness) fails at a closed point. The introduction states the conjecture with 'locally free tangent sheaf'. Global freeness is a stronger hypothesis than local freeness, so the same example refutes that form too. The text also gives the analytic germ (the complex-space version) and the local ring A_m, whose derivations are free (Der_C(T) ≅ T^d in the proof). The text states that Spec A can be chosen smooth away from m. Normality of A is consistent with Lipman's theorem, which the introduction cites as showing that free derivations force normality.

The introduction cites van Straten and Steenbrink as proving the isolated-singularity case in dimension at least three, so any higher-dimensional counterexample must have non-isolated singularities, and the manuscript does not treat that. disputes.summary: Graded case: Hochster (1977) is credited in the Encyclopaedia of Mathematics and by Hochster's bibliography; Biswas–Gurjar–Kolte credit Platte (1978) for the graded analytic case, starting from Hochster's algebraic work. A search summary also credits Avramov and Herzog with solving the graded case. These are different results or credits, not one result claimed twice.

Nakai implies Zariski–Lipman: a search summary attributes this to Becker and Rego; the Wikipedia Nakai article (opened) states the implication without naming who proved it, and cites Becker (1977). Not confirmed from Becker's text.

Graf's 'generalized Lipman–Zariski' paper (arXiv:1405.1244): the arXiv record's latest version is v3 of 16 Oct 2014. One indexed PDF rendering carries a date of 3 Dec 2024, and a search summary described a 2024 Graf paper on higher exterior powers. I could not find that preprint, and the arXiv author page returned 404. Treated as an indexing artefact, not an event.

A search summary described a 2026 Graf paper showing that Lipman's counterexample is the only rational double point violating the conjecture in characteristic p ≥ 7. The paper that says this is Graf's arXiv:2201.06646 (January 2022), and no 2026 paper was found. Not recorded as an event.

Barajas et al. (arXiv:2510.07607): one search summary says the paper discusses a Zariski–Lipman counterexample; the abstract page does not mention the conjecture; the PDF was unreadable. Left unresolved.

summary: I ran 38 WebSearch queries and opened abstract and reference pages for about 22 sources; the PDFs of the two in-window papers and several others could not be read through my tools. Every status statement I read for the statement itself calls it open in general: the Encyclopaedia of Mathematics entry (last major progress as of 2000), the Wikipedia Nakai article (which the bullet's Zariski–Lipman link redirects to; it calls Nakai's conjecture unproven and says a proof of it would establish the Zariski–Lipman conjecture), and an undated Emergent Mind open-problem page. The record therefore has two layers. Pre-2024 partial results are recorded as events, each with its scope: dimension one and normality (Lipman 1965, as cited); hypersurfaces (Scheja–Storch 1972, as cited); the graded case (Hochster 1977) and the graded analytic case (Platte 1978, as cited); locally complete intersections (Källström 2010, rewritten 2018, after an error was found in the earlier versions); klt spaces (Greb–Kebekus–Kovács–Peternell, arXiv 2010, as claimed in the abstract); log canonical spaces (Druel 2013, with Graf–Kovács 2013 conditional and Heuver 2015 as a second proof); a commuting-vector-field case (Jörder 2013); surfaces (Biswas–Gurjar–Kolte 2014, classes unnamed in the abstract; Graf 2018 for genus one; Bergner–Graf 2019 for p_g − g − b ≤ 2); complete intersections with singular locus of codimension at least 3 (Miller–Vassiliadou 2019); toric varieties (Tipler 2022). The in-window items are two. (i) Nascimento, Jorge-Pérez and Freitas (arXiv 2405.06745, 10 May 2024) give a conditional criterion for the ring-theoretic version, under a Betti-number condition on Der_k(R) that is not shown to hold for any class; I record it as conditional, not as a case. (ii) Barajas, Chávez-Martínez and Romano-Velázquez (arXiv 2510.07607, 8 Oct 2025) are about resolution by blowing up the derivation module; their abstract does not mention the conjecture, and one search summary says the full text does. I could not read the PDF, so this stays unresolved. Close calls: whether a conditional criterion counts as moving a quantity the statement asks about (the statement asks for the implication in general, so I read it as not settling anything); whether the 2025 paper bears on the statement at all; whether the unnamed Biswas–Gurjar–Kolte surface classes amount to a case. Items discarded with reasons: Graf 2014's p = 2 counterexample (a different problem: reflexive p-forms with p ≠ 1); Graf 2022's violations (characteristic p); Brumatti et al. 2002 counterexamples (non-finite-type class); Jorge-Pérez and Miranda-Neto 2021 (strong, finite-projective-dimension version); Hochster's proposed counterexample (announced in a 2020 talk abstract, with no construction found). AI involvement: none found for any event. The abstract of AlphaProof Nexus (arXiv 2605.22763, opened) names no problem and does not mention Zariski or Lipman. The 'AlphaProof Nexus algebraic geometry' item is a 15-year-old question about Hilbert functions; a secondary wiki snippet identifies it as Zanello's log-concavity conjecture for pure O-sequences, not this conjecture (that wiki page returned 429 and was not opened). Other AI-credited algebraic geometry results I saw concern different problems: the Jacobian conjecture (credited to Claude in secondary sources) and the Yau–Tian–Donaldson counterexample (a 2026 preprint, from a search summary). Their absence from this record is deliberate. The AI check on the older events rests on abstracts and bibliographic records, and where I did not read the full text it is a chronological fact (the paper predates any AI system named in this project) plus an absence of any named system in what I read.
competing_reading: The strongest case for counting something in the window: Nascimento, Jorge-Pérez and Freitas (May 2024) give the first stated general criterion for the ring-theoretic Zariski–Lipman conjecture in the period, and Barajas et al. (October 2025) may treat the conjecture in full text, as one search summary says. The case against: the criterion is conditional on an unverified Betti-number hypothesis, the 2025 abstract does not mention the conjecture, and every status statement I read still calls the conjecture open in general.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The theorem and hypotheses of arXiv 2405.06745, read from a text version of the PDF, and whether any ring class is shown to satisfy the condition. (2) The full text of arXiv 2510.07607, to see whether it discusses the Zariski–Lipman conjecture and in which direction. (3) Becker (1977) and Platte (1978) themselves, to confirm the Nakai implication and the graded analytic credit. (4) Hochster's proposed counterexample, from Gurjar's talk notes or Part 2, to see whether it is a valid characteristic-zero construction. (5) Lipman (1965) to confirm the normality and dimension-one claims directly. (6) The formal-conjectures repository and the AlphaProof Nexus paper's problem list, to rule the conjecture in or out of the AI-system work. (7) A citation search of post-2024 papers for the Druel, Bergner–Graf and Tipler results, to check later_work_cites_it fields that I left null.

event.what_happened: The family is a single manuscript, 'A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf'. The argument has two steps. (1) Proposition 'analytic-counterexample' builds a normal complex surface germ (X,x), smooth off x, with free holomorphic tangent sheaf of rank two. It takes a smooth genus-21 curve C with normal bundle L⁻¹, deg L = 10, L⁴ ≅ K_C; prescribes finite jets of two vector fields on a neighbourhood of C by finitely many holomorphic flows; glues these to a Hausdorff surface neighbourhood Y of C; lifts the jets holomorphically using vanishing of H¹ on the ideal filtration; and contracts C to x by Grauert's criterion. The text gives C² = −10, canonical discrepancy −5 for C, and p_g ≥ 33 (Remark 'invariants'). (2) Proposition 'algebraization' produces an affine normal A with the same completed local ring as (X,x) at the marked point, a principal affine neighbourhood on which Der_C(A) ≅ A^d with d = 2, and smoothness away from that point. The proof uses a finite-determinacy lemma with a relation matrix, which the paper proves itself, together with Artin approximation over a henselization.

judgement.why: The statement is a single universal implication over C, so a valid characteristic-zero affine counterexample answers all of it: the OpenAI manuscript claims a normal affine surface with Der_C(A) free of rank two and singular, which is scope whole, direction refuted, object a counterexample (non-explicit, so not checkable), unreviewed after 8 days. I kept it as doubtful rather than credible because the record names compressed and self-proved key steps, but no identified error, so it is not set aside. AI role is generated on the README's statement that results were obtained with the internal model; the manuscript lists no human authors. The two other in-window papers are a conditional criterion and an unrelated blow-up paper (none). Pre-snapshot partial results are cases with journal publication counted as digested; analytic-only, characteristic-p, non-finite-type, finite-projective-dimension and added-hypothesis (commuting basis) results are variants. Analytic surface-singularity results (Graf 2018, Bergner–Graf) were read as cases because the analytic germ class contains the algebraic one; Platte's analytic graded result is a variant since Hochster already covers the algebraic graded case.
judgement.doubts: The OpenAI README quote is generic for the repository ('the vast majority of results'), not specific to family 048; generated rests on it plus the absence of human authors. The counterexample's validity hinges on the freeness-descent step through Artin approximation, which the record itself flags. Several pre-snapshot 'digested' calls rest on journal publication known only from search summaries.
